text.p: Nestle SA said that its sales for the first 10 months of 1996 rose 5.7 percent to 48.3 billion Swiss francs.
In the comparable 1995 period, sales were 45.7 billion Swiss francs.
In a press release accompanying its 10-month results, Nestle said sales volume grew 3.0 percent, a slight slowdown from the 3.6 percent growth reported for the first half.

"This slight slowdown of growth is largely due to bad weather conditions in Europe in August and September, which naturally had a negative impact on sales of mineral water and ice cream," Nestle said.
"On the other hand, encouraging growth continued in soluble coffee," it said.
Separately, Nestle said sales from its joint venture with General Mills Inc, called Cereal Partners Worldwide, rose 23 percent to 689 million Swiss francs in the first 10 months of 1996.
Sales from the Galderma joint venture with French beauty products group L'Oreal were up 37 percent to 202 million francs.
Nestle said these were total sales of which it books 50 percent.
